newsitem.title: GERMANY: Beef consumption down 10-15 pct in EU - Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Beef consumption down 10-15 pct in EU - Bonn.

text.p: Beef consumption has dropped by between 10 and 15 percent in the European Union as a whole and by 15-20 percent in Germany since the start of the year, the Bonn farm ministry said on Monday.

The German government planned measures to help restore consumer confidence and aid farmers hit by the so-called mad cow beef scare, a ministry circular quoted state secretary Wolfgang Groebl as saying in response to a parliamentary question.

These included planned subsidies for the private storage of beef earmarked for export, talks with East European countries on a reduction in their calf sales to the EU and better labelling and consumer information on meat products.

German producers had benefited more than others from EU beef intervention, or support, purchases since April 1996. Buying in Germany accounted for a third of the 340,000 tonne EU total to date, Groebl said.
The government was committed to supporting further intervention buying, but would seek to prevent massive stockbuilding by offering premiums for quick sales to the free market.
Beef stocks were virtually down to zero before the mad cow crisis erupted in March.
